events.title: An LLM judge scores the day's conversations
events.detail: It pulls every trace from Langfuse and scores task completion, tool-call efficiency, and response quality. Against my own labels it scored near chance, so its scores sort what I look at; they don't decide anything.

events.title: Backups snapshot, then sync
events.detail: The SQLite databases get an atomic snapshot instead of a raw file copy, then sync to two separate recovery destinations. Each run reports its own result, so a failed backup shows up the same day.

events.title: The agent drafts edits to its own prompt
events.detail: It clusters the last 30 days of low-scoring turns and proposes specific prompt edits. They go to Telegram and are never applied automatically.

events.title: New llama.cpp commits get read before they land
events.detail: Upstream moves fast enough to break this exact AMD hardware path, so new commits are reviewed before the build moves forward.

events.title: I approve or reject each proposed edit
events.detail: Approval is a real command: `apply 1 2` lands specific proposals, `skip improvements` declines the batch. In one real run I approved two of three; the third would have fixed the wrong thing.
